PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION:
Description of Proposal – Safe Skies Evaluation Trailer (Form 7460-1)
Safe Skies proposes the temporary deployment of a mobile trailer to support an upcoming security technology evaluation. The trailer is required on-site due to bandwidth limitations preventing effective remote operation.

Purpose of the Trailer:
The trailer will house network and evaluation equipment and will serve as a platform to mount pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras on a 20-foot (AGL) mast. No radar transmission equipment will be installed on the mast.

Proposed Location and Coordinates:

• Latitude/Longitude: 38°51'39\N / 77°02'13"W

• The proposed site ensures the trailer is positioned at least 10 feet inside the perimeter fence and does not obstruct access roads or the boat ramp gate.

• The front of the trailer will be approximately 30 feet south of the boat ramp gate.

• The mast location is identified by a red dot in the attached schematic and will be approximately 25 feet west of the perimeter fence.

Structure Details:

• Structure Type: Mast on trailer

• Structure Height: 20 feet above ground level (AGL)

• Total Footprint: Trailer and associated Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)

• Guy Wire Clearance: The mast will be supported by three guy wires  each extending approximately 12 feet from the base in a radial pattern. All guy wire anchors will remain well clear of the perimeter fence and boat ramp access.

Power Supply:
The trailer will be powered by an adjacent Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The schematic includes the BESS footprint within the overall trailer setup.

Operational Duration:
This is a temporary installation to support a specific technology evaluation program under Safe Skies. The trailer and mast will be removed upon completion of the evaluation.

Obstruction Review Justification:
The temporary structure does not interfere with any established roadways or gates  remains within controlled property boundaries  and stays below FAA height thresholds for permanent structures.

PROPOSAL DESCRIPTION: PRPA has plans to construct a new cruise terminal at #4 Hog Island Road along the Delaware River.  The site has an existing pier that can provide access to a cruise ship for embarking and departing of passengers  luggage  and supplies.  The project scope / basis of design includes a new 48 000 square foot cruise terminal building and site development for the following: a drop-off areas for buses  Taxis  Ubers  a 300 000 square foot parking lot  widening of the roads  and covered islands for car pick-up.  The new cruise terminal building approximately 578 feet long x 83 feet wide  and is proposed to be located directly adjacent to the pier.  Site demolition will be limited existing buildings and accessory structures and existing railroad ties than are in conflict with the proposed building footprint  drop off lane and incoming bus parking areas.The cruise terminal building construction is proposed to be an insulated fabric exterior membrane attached to a pre-engineered steel structure.  The building steel columns would be supported and anchored to a structural concrete slab and foundation.  The proposed building foundation system includes concrete spread footings  perimeter grade walls with continuous footings  and interior floor slabs with control joints.  The finished floor of the terminal building will be set equal to the top of the adjacent dock  which is approximately 3’-0” above final grade.   The cruise terminal building will include mechanical heating  ventilation  air conditioning (HVAC)  plumbing  fire protection  and electrical components.  The attached Concept Sketch depicts the proposed building location on the site layout and overall project scope of work.  The sketch was developed by Bowman Consulting Group  who is the engineering firm restoring the pier.
LOCATION DESCRIPTION: The site is located at #4 Hog Island Road  Philadelphia  PA and is currently owned by Energy Transfer.  There is a paved access road off Fort Mifflin Road / Hog Island Road to access the site. The majority of the site is abandoned  with four buildings either unoccupied or not-in-use. The site is paved  relatively flat  and there are some wetlands adjacent to the vegetated  undeveloped areas.  There are signs of existing utilities below the vegetated areas. The site provides access to an existing pier  over 1 000 feet in length  located on the Delaware River.  There are adjacent structures / buildings within a mile radius such as the the Philadelphia International Airport  the UPS Cargo Building  Menzies Aviation PHL Fuel Facility and Sunoco Logistics.  The site is located south of the Philadelphia International Airport.

This filing is for the mobile crane used to erect 1 of 2 tower cranes on site. ASN 2025-AEA-8511-OE.  The mobile crane is a LIEBHERR LTM1650-8.1.  The mobile crane will not reach heights above 317 feet including most upper parts of the crane.
